title: Long TBT — Warsh FOMC Hawkish Re-Entry at T3 Breakout
entry: Enter $43-47 (TBT is trading at the T3-breakout level of the prior TBT position, which closed all three targets). Scale: 60% at first entry in the $43-46 zone; add 40% on any post-Warsh dip to $43-44 on June 17 — if press conference language spooks markets, TBT may give back 2-3% intraday before resuming. Do NOT add above $47 unless 30Y closes decisively above 5.20%.
stop_loss: $40 daily close (~11% below $45 midpoint) — implies Warsh June 17 adopts explicitly dovish language with rate-cut guidance for 2026, OR 30Y falls below 4.80% on sustained flight-to-safety bid that overrides the hawkish narrative
targets: $49 — 30Y at 5.20%; Warsh June 17 signals July rate-hike probability above 60% explicitly; bear steepening continues; +8.9% from $45 midpoint
$54 — 30Y at 5.35%+; Warsh delivers June 17 hike OR signals July delivery with explicit inflation data justification; Goldman 'first cut June 2027' validated by FOMC communications; +20.0%
$60 — 30Y at 5.50%; July FOMC hike confirmed; bear steepening regime formally established; structural short-bond thesis pays in full; +33.3%
catalyst: The prior TBT position (long-tbt-nfp-fomc-hike-reload-2026-06-01) hit all three targets, closing today at T3 ($43) with TBT at $44-46. FOMC Day 1 is June 16; Warsh press conference June 17 at 2:30 PM ET. The rate-hike backdrop is fully intact: Goldman Sachs calls no 2026 cuts (first cut June 2027), 20% probability of a June hike is priced in derivatives, and 30Y is holding above 4.90% ahead of the meeting. The prior TBT entry of $34.80-36.50 was calibrated to 30Y at 4.95-5.05%; re-entry at $43-47 reflects the new equilibrium after the regime shift confirmed by all three prior targets being hit.
thesis:
TBT's breakout through T3 ($43) is confirmation — not conclusion — of a structural yield-regime shift. The prior TBT position validated the thesis mechanically: from entry $35.77 to $44+, a 20%+ gain as 30Y moved from 4.95% toward 4.90-4.91%. The re-entry at $43-47 is a continuation trade in a confirmed trend. Three structural pillars underpin continued TBT appreciation: the Fed's hawkish institutional baseline, the fiscal supply overhang, and the post-Iran-deal growth reacceleration.

The Fed's hawkish baseline enters June 17 explicitly intact. The 8-4 voting split from the April FOMC minutes gives Warsh the institutional support to signal a rate hike without unanimous consensus. Goldman Sachs — the FOMC's most-watched external forecaster — has publicly called no 2026 cuts and first cut June 2027, aligning their macro forecast with the market's hawkish interpretation. The 20% rate-hike tail probability embedded in swaptions is cheap optionality: if Warsh hikes, TBT jumps 6-8% in a session; if he holds with hawkish guidance, TBT gains 3-5% on forward path re-pricing.

The fiscal supply overhang is the structural driver that keeps 30Y elevated independent of short-term Fed communication. Treasury issuance in H2 2026 is projected at $900B+ as the deficit financing cycle continues. The 30Y term premium was negative for most of 2024 and has now normalized positive — a regime shift that is structural, not cyclical. This means 30Y yields have a natural upward bias absent a strong growth shock.

The post-Iran peace deal adds a hawkish dynamic: lower oil reduces the stagflation recessionary channel, removing one of the few arguments for near-term cuts. A growth-positive peace deal that lowers energy costs is net-hawkish for the Fed's inflation path — the labor market-driven inflation pressure becomes the dominant signal with energy risk removed. The bull-case tail (Warsh hikes June 17) is low probability but the payoff is outsized; the base case (hawkish hold with July guidance) still drives TBT 8-10% higher.
bull_case: Warsh June 17 hikes 25bps and signals another possible by September 'if inflation progress stalls.' 30Y to 5.20% immediately; TBT gaps from $45 to $50 on the day. June PCE (released late June) prints above 3.0% core — third consecutive above-target reading — sealing July hike probability above 80%. 30Y to 5.35%; TBT to $54 (Target 2) within 3 weeks. Tail: Treasury announces Q3 refunding with above-consensus 30Y supply; term premium widens further and TBT reaches $60 by August.
bear_case: Warsh June 17 holds but is unexpectedly dovish: 'The FOMC sees a path to rate cuts later this year if inflation moderates.' Market interprets this as December 2026 cut probability rising. 30Y falls 15-20bps to 4.72-4.75%; TBT drops to $40 (stop triggered). Alternatively: Iran peace deal creates a growth boom that pulls SPX to 7,800+, triggering a 'growth is back' narrative where the bond market rallies on reduced deficit financing expectations — a counterintuitive but real tail risk.
invalidation: $40 daily close, OR Warsh June 17 press conference contains explicit rate-cut timing guidance for 2026, OR 30Y falls below 4.80% and holds for 3 consecutive sessions, OR Goldman Sachs reverses their 'no 2026 cut' call
